messages:
alex.cs: FYI customer ACME hitting intermittent 429s during a bulk embeddings job last night. They gave two request-ids: req_01F3A9 and req_01F3B0. Need repro evidence + debug bundle.

kevin.support: Can you paste the raw headers + a minimal curl? Also which endpoint and model were they calling?

alex.cs: Endpoint: POST /v1/embeddings  model: text-embedding-3-small  region: us-east-1  time: 2025-11-02T18:22:45Z
Request-IDs: req_01F3A9, req_01F3B0
Headers (from customer response):
```
x-rate-limit-limit: 60
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 32
retry-after: 32
request-id: req_01F3A9
```
Log snippet from their client (redacted):
```
2025-11-02T18:22:44Z - POST /v1/embeddings - status:200 - id:req_01F3A8
2025-11-02T18:22:45Z - POST /v1/embeddings - status:429 - id:req_01F3A9 - body: {"error":"rate limit"}
2025-11-02T18:22:46Z - POST /v1/embeddings - status:429 - id:req_01F3B0 - body: {"error":"rate limit"}
```

kevin.support: Try this minimal reproducer (use a redacted token). Run in a tight loop to emulate burst: 
```
for i in {1..200}; do \
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{size_download}" \
    -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"text-embedding-3-small","input":"test"}'; \
  sleep 0.1;
done
```

maria.dev: Ask the customer for their client pattern: are they doing Promise.all or a serial loop? If they used Promise.all over 200 items that will spike concurrency. Recommend concurrency limit + exponential backoff.

sam.sre: I'll pull server traces for those request-ids. @deploy-bot can you create a debug bundle for ACME around 2025-11-02T18:22Z? Need traces, proxy logs, and rate-limit aggregator logs.

deploy-bot: debug-bundle created: https://internal-debug.redwood/bundles/1750001250-acme-20251102.zip (expires in 7d)

kevin.support: I ran the reproducer against staging with 0.1s sleep. Reproduced 429 at ~62nd request within 60s. Response headers on the 429: `x-rate-limit-limit: 60`, `x-rate-limit-remaining: 0`, `x-rate-limit-reset: 28`, `retry-after: 28`, `request-id: req_stg_9c2`. Timeline: successes 1-61, 62 -> 429.

alex.cs: Customer confirmed their client retried immediately with no backoff; they were using Promise.all on batches of 200. I'm asking them to try concurrency=8 and exponential backoff (jitter). Sending them the debug bundle link.

maria.dev: This looks like hitting the per-key token quota rather than an upstream issue. Short-term options: advise client to throttle or we can temporarily increase their quota for the Dedicated trial. Also action: add a note in SDK docs about concurrency and 429-handling patterns.

sam.sre: Action items: 1) Kevin attach full reproducer logs here. 2) Alex to coordinate customer code change and retest. 3) Maria to draft SDK retry guidance and add a snippet. I'll watch server-side 429 rates for 24h and open a capacity follow-up if sustained.

kevin.support: Reproducer output (sanitized):
```
200 512
200 512
... (success x61) ...
429 85  <-- headers: x-rate-limit-limit:60, x-rate-limit-remaining:0, retry-after:28, request-id:req_stg_9c2
429 85
```
:thumbsup:

alex.cs: Thanks all — I sent instructions to ACME and requested updated client logs after they switch to concurrency=8. Marking thread in-progress; will update by EOD with results.

kevin.support: If they still see repeated 429 spikes after client changes, we'll open a capacity escalation with infra. For now, evidence shows burst pattern + per-key quota enforcement.

maria.dev: Adding docs TODO: "Handling 429s and safe concurrency" and linking reproducer.

sam.sre: Closing loop once customer confirms. If we see any 5xxs tied to the incidents, escalate immediately.

alex.cs: Closing note: requested their full debug bundle and client stack trace. Keeping this thread as the single source. Will tag again when they respond. :white_check_mark:
